## Overview

`causalInferencePipeline()` pairs QTL fine-mapping and/or regularized
regression weights with one or more GWAS studies to produce two kinds of
row, told apart by the `analysis` column:

- **TWAS rows** (`"twas"`): a TWAS Z-score and p-value per chosen
    `(qtlStudy, context, trait, method)` weight set and GWAS study, and
-  when `fineMappingResult` is supplied, **MR rows** (`"mr"`): a
    Mendelian Randomization Wald-ratio estimate over the QTL credible sets,
    per fine-mapping row and GWAS study.

Three valid input combinations:

| What you supply | TWAS-Z source | MR? |
|---|---|---|
| `twasWeights` only | per-tuple weights from `TwasWeights` | no |
| `fineMappingResult` only | SuSiE coefficients from `topLoci()` | yes |
| both | weights from `TwasWeights` | yes, from the fine-mapping result alone |

MR is driven by the fine-mapping result only: every gene and fine-mapping
method it holds is estimated against every GWAS study it overlaps,
whichever TWAS methods were chosen and whether or not `twasWeights` holds
the gene. A fine-mapping method among the TWAS weights, such as `susie`, is
a TWAS method like any other; MR never reads it.

```{r load-packages}
library(pecotmr)
```

## Bundled inputs

```{r bundled}
data(qtlDatasetExample, gwasSumStatsS4Example)

# Pre-compute the QTL-side products from the bundled QtlDataset.
# crossValidation carries the per-fold susie fits to the weights pipeline,
# which never fine-maps for itself.
fmr <- fineMappingPipeline(
    qtlDatasetExample,
    methods = "susie",
    cisWindow = 1e6,
    crossValidationParam = CrossValidationParam(folds = 3)
)
tw <- twasWeightsPipeline(
    qtlDatasetExample,
    methods = "susie",
    cisWindow = 1e6,
    fineMappingResult = fmr
)
```

## TWAS Z only (weights alone)

```{r ci-tw-only}
res <- causalInferencePipeline(
    gwasSumStats = gwasSumStatsS4Example,
    twasWeights = tw
)
head(S4Vectors::mcols(res))
```

The result is a `GRanges` object positioned at the variant span of each QTL
weight set, with identity columns (`qtlStudy`, `context`, `trait`,
`method`, `gwasStudy`), `analysis`, and the TWAS columns (`twasZ`,
`twasPval`). With weights alone every row is a TWAS row, and its MR columns
are `NA`.

## Choosing TWAS methods

`weightSelectionParam` picks which methods' weights are scored for each
gene, from the cross-validation metrics the weights carry, through
`WeightSelectionParam(methods =)`:

- `"best"` (the default): each gene's method with the highest CV r-squared
    whose weights are not all zero.
- `"all"`: every method.
- method names, e.g. `c("lasso", "mrash")`: those methods.

`cutoff` (CV r-squared) and `pvalCutoff` (CV p-value) bound every choice.
A gene whose methods carry no CV metric keeps them all, there being nothing
to rank them by. The choice reads the weights alone, never a GWAS study, so
`ctwasPipeline()` makes the same one from the same settings.

```{r ci-methods, eval=FALSE}
causalInferencePipeline(
    gwasSumStats = gwasSumStatsS4Example,
    twasWeights = tw,
    weightSelectionParam = WeightSelectionParam(methods = "all", cutoff = 0.01)
)
```

## TWAS Z + MR (weights + fine-mapping)

When you also pass `fineMappingResult`, the pipeline adds Wald-ratio MR
rows to the TWAS rows. The MR uses each fine-mapping entry's `topLoci` rows
as candidate instrumental variables, and its row's `method` is the
fine-mapping method.

```{r ci-both}
res2 <- causalInferencePipeline(
    gwasSumStats = gwasSumStatsS4Example,
    twasWeights = tw,
    fineMappingResult = fmr,
    mrParam = MrParam(method = "ivwPerVariant", pipCutoff = 0.5)
)
S4Vectors::mcols(res2)[, c(
    "method",
    "analysis",
    "twasZ",
    "twasPval",
    "waldRatio",
    "waldRatioSe",
    "mrPval",
    "nIV"
)]
```

## MR variants: per-variant vs CS-aware IVW

| `MrParam(method=)` | What it does | Extra filters |
|---|---|---|
| `"ivwPerVariant"` (default) | Treats every `topLoci` variant with `pip > pipCutoff` as an IV; pools their Wald ratios via inverse-variance weighting. | `pipCutoff` |
| `"csAware"` | Groups variants by credible set (column `cs` in `topLoci`), forms a PIP-weighted composite Wald ratio per CS (subject to per-CS cumulative-PIP cutoff `cpipCutoff`), then IVW-pools across CSs. Reports Cochran's Q and I-squared. | `cpipCutoff` |

```{r ci-csaware, eval=FALSE}
causalInferencePipeline(
    gwasSumStats = gwasSumStatsS4Example,
    twasWeights = tw,
    fineMappingResult = fmr,
    mrParam = MrParam(method = "csAware", cpipCutoff = 0.5)
)
```

## Cross-method p-value combination

When a `(qtlStudy, context, trait, gwasStudy)` group has TWAS results
from multiple weight methods, `combineMethods` runs
`combinePValues()` to produce a single combined p-value per group. The
default choice scores one method per gene, so combination wants
`methods = "all"` or several named methods.

```{r ci-combine, eval=FALSE}
# Multi-method weights so combination is meaningful
tw_multi <- twasWeightsPipeline(
    qtlDatasetExample,
    methods = c("susie", "lasso")
)
causalInferencePipeline(
    gwasSumStats = gwasSumStatsS4Example,
    twasWeights = tw_multi,
    weightSelectionParam = WeightSelectionParam(methods = "all"),
    combineMethods = c("acat", "hmp")
)
```

Accepted values for `combineMethods`: `acat`, `hmp`,
`bonferroni`, `fisher`, `stouffer`, `invchisq`, `gbj`, `bj`, `hc`,
`ghc`, `minp`, `gbj_omni`, `aspu`, `gates` (see `?combinePValues`).

The per-tuple p-value itself comes from `waldTestPval()`, which is exported
so the same test can be applied to any effect estimate and standard error:

```{r wald}
waldTestPval(beta = 2.5, se = 0.8, n = 10000)
```

`n` sets the degrees of freedom, so a small study gives a more conservative
p-value than the normal approximation would.

## LD reference consistency

Both `twasWeights` and `fineMappingResult` record an LD reference per row.
Where a row has one, it must be the same LD reference as the `gwasSumStats`
rows it overlaps carry. The pipeline errors on mismatch.

A QTL row with no LD reference (e.g. weights learned from individual-level
data without any RSS step) skips the panel check — useful for analyses that
mix individual-level QTL fits with sumstats GWAS.

## Common parameters

```{r ci-params, eval=FALSE}
causalInferencePipeline(
    gwasSumStats = gwasSumStatsS4Example,
    twasWeights = tw,
    fineMappingResult = fmr,
    weightSelectionParam = WeightSelectionParam(methods = "best"),
    mrParam = MrParam(
        method = "ivwPerVariant",
        pipCutoff = 0.5, # cpipCutoff instead, for method = "csAware"
        pvalCutoff = 1 # estimate MR only for genes with a TWAS p below this
    ),
    combineMethods = NULL
) # e.g. c("acat", "hmp")
```

## Reading the result

The `GRanges` output indexes results by the QTL variant span: a TWAS row
sits at the span of its weights' variants the GWAS holds, and an MR row at
the span of its fine-mapping row's variants. Extract per-tuple values with
`S4Vectors::mcols()`:

```{r ci-mcols, eval=FALSE}
mc <- as.data.frame(S4Vectors::mcols(res2))
twasRows <- mc[mc$analysis == "twas", ]
# Significant TWAS hits at Bonferroni alpha = 0.05 across TWAS rows
twasRows[twasRows$twasPval < 0.05 / nrow(twasRows), ]
```
